_readme: STARTER PACK — authored to be REPLACED by upstream. JSON has no comment syntax, so this
key is the header comment; the loader ignores unknown keys.
Nobody at Sparkle is an authority on what the law says. The HumaneBench project and
community are expected to define and maintain the real packs; this exists so the
mechanism has something to run against on day one.
Every 'guidance' string below is a NON-AUTHORITATIVE PLAIN-LANGUAGE PARAPHRASE. The
'source' URL governs.
THE DATES MATTER HERE AND ARE THE PACK AUTHOR'S READING OF ART. 113. The Act applies in
stages: the Art. 5 prohibitions from 2 Feb 2025; Chapter IV — which contains ALL of
Art. 50, both 50(1) and 50(2) — from 2 Aug 2026; and the Art. 6(1) high-risk
classification rules with their Chapter III obligations from 2 Aug 2027.
Art. 50(2) is dated 2 Aug 2026 with the rest of Chapter IV. Its marking duty is
conditioned on technical feasibility and on harmonised standards still in development,
but that is a question about what the duty REQUIRES, not about when it applies, and a
later date here would make every citation say 'Not yet in force' about a duty that is.
Confirm every date against the source before relying on it — that is exactly what the
citation asks counsel to do.
There is no deterministic detector for either Art. 50 duty — whether a disclosure is
adequate, or whether output is marked machine-readably, is a judgement about the whole
product rather than a string match. Both are therefore authored as JUDGED checks. The
loader REJECTS a pack naming an unregistered detector, so a check can no longer point at
a detector that does not exist and sit silent forever.
This pack never asserts compliance. A check that does not fire means nothing fired —
not that a product is lawful.

REMOVED 2026-08-22: a speculative Art. 6 / Annex III high-risk check. It was added only to exercise the future-dated advisory path against shipped data, and it was wrong twice over — Annex III classification is Art. 6(2), not 6(1), and its date was a guess. It also asked about a CLASSIFICATION rather than an unmet duty, so unlike every other check here it would fire on any AI-touching PR instead of only when something is wrong. Shipping a legal claim we are not sure of is exactly what this pack format exists to avoid; the advisory mechanism is covered by fixture tests and needs no shipped example.
notice: Guidance text is a non-authoritative paraphrase and the effective dates are the pack author's reading of the Act's staged applicability; the source URL governs.

checks.title: People must be told they are interacting with an AI system

detect.question: Does this change put a person into direct interaction with an AI system — a chat, an assistant, a generated reply, a synthetic voice — without telling them so, in a situation where it would not already be obvious to a reasonably well-informed person?

checks.guidance: that a person interacting with an AI system be informed of that fact, unless it is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person in the circumstances

checks.title: Synthetic content must be marked as machine-readable

detect.question: Does this change emit synthetic audio, image, video or text to people without marking it in a machine-readable format as artificially generated or manipulated?

checks.guidance: that synthetic audio, image, video or text output be marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated, so far as that is technically feasible

checks.title: No subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques

detect.question: Does this change use subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques that materially distort a person's behaviour and impair their ability to make an informed decision — for example a countdown, a shamed decline button, or a hidden default?

checks.guidance: that an AI system not deploy subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques that materially distort behaviour and cause or are likely to cause significant harm

checks.title: No exploitation of age, disability or social or economic situation

detect.question: Does this change exploit a vulnerability arising from a person's age, disability, or social or economic situation in order to distort their behaviour?

checks.guidance: that an AI system not exploit vulnerabilities of age, disability, or a specific social or economic situation in a way that materially distorts behaviour and causes or is likely to cause significant harm
